title: Policy for component and flow identity
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want a policy for graph identity (components and data-flows) that does not hide naming misses and does not make every corpus run look like 0% recall.

## Current contract (intentional)

`identitiesMatch` requires **exact** `subject.key` for components and data-flows. We explicitly did not alias `third_party:checkr` to `asset:requests call`. That is a scanner naming/classification issue.

Gold was written as human taxonomy (`third_party:checkr`, `flow:pii->checkr-api`, `asset:database`). The engine emits detector names (`asset:django orm`, `asset:requests call`, `flow:asset:…->asset:…`). On vgs-django after the harness fix, component and flow recall were 0% with 0 unread. That is an honest miss **if** we believe gold keys are the product identity.

## Why it blocks scanner work

If we start “improving the scanner” from those zeros, every session will retune third-party heuristics and flow wiring. That may be right — or the gold identity convention (`type:lowercase name`) may be the thing that should move, or we need a **naming grade** separate from “did we detect an HTTP client at all.”

Putting vendor aliases into `identity.ts` would make Checkr look solved while the engine still does not know Checkr. Using 0% as a gate with no `documentedGap` will drown PII/data-item signal.

Labels have the same split: gold `database` / `data_flow` vs finding `[asset, subtype]` / `api_call`. We already special-case some of that in `labelsMatch`. That is another policy, not a detector bug.

## Questions to answer

- Are gold component keys a stable public identity the engine must emit, or a reviewer’s nickname that adapters may map?
- If the engine must emit gold keys, how do we mark today’s naming misses (`documentedGap`, a naming sub-score, per-vendor allowlists) so recall is usable?
- If adapters may map, what is the *closed* map (not “any HTTP client matches any third_party”)?
- Flows: gold `flow:pii->checkr-api` vs `flow:${componentIdentity}->${componentIdentity}`. Same question as components, because flow identity is defined in terms of component identity.
- Exact span overlap on flows whose `sourceLocations` are empty or only on one endpoint: match, unread, or exclude from precision?

## Not this task

Do not add Checkr-specific detector rules to make vgs-django green while this policy is open.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Decision

Components and flows use structured canonical graph identities rather than opaque exact strings or permissive aliases.

A component expectation separates type, taxonomy subtype, canonical instance/vendor when known, and supporting evidence. The component taxonomy is authoritative for type and subtype. The scorer produces one strict all-required-fields result plus diagnostics for observation detection, type/subtype classification, and instance/vendor resolution. Thus `asset:requests call` at Checkr evidence can show partial detection while remaining a strict miss for the Checkr component; the naming/classification failure is not hidden.

Mappings into canonical component fields must be closed, reviewed, versioned, and evidence-backed. Category-wide aliases such as any HTTP client matching any third party are forbidden.

A flow is a structured typed edge. Its endpoints reference canonical component/data entities or typed endpoint identities, and its data categories are separate fields. Human strings such as `flow:pii->checkr-api` are display forms, not scorer identity. Flow reporting distinguishes topology detection, endpoint resolution, semantic classification, and the strict complete match. This permits useful attribution without making an unresolved vendor look solved.

Graph precision uses an explicitly reviewed packet-and-layer graph scope. File overlap alone is insufficient for repository graph entities. Findings must carry derivation provenance where possible. Locationless or otherwise unscorable graph findings are counted and reported as unscorable; they are never silently omitted from the headline report. A follow-on contract may gate on maximum unscorable rate.

`documentedGap` is release-gate policy, not ground truth. Raw recall always includes the miss. Any temporary gate exception records an issue, owner, reason, and expiry and is listed beside the gate-adjusted result.

Rejected alternatives:

- vendor aliases in the identity matcher;
- exact comparison of overloaded human-authored key strings as the only signal;
- allowing partial detection to count as a strict success;
- excluding known gaps from raw metrics;
- silently dropping locationless graph findings from precision.

Detector and Checkr-specific improvements remain out of scope until this contract is implemented.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
_Review pass recorded before the contract decisions were posted; kept for provenance. Where it conflicts with a decision, the decision governs — the follow-up comment below reconciles the two._

## This is not a naming policy — the component taxonomy is half-adopted

The description says gold was written as human taxonomy and the engine emits detector names, and treats the gap as a naming/classification issue to be graded or aliased. The data says something narrower and more fixable.

### What component gold actually contains

563 annotations, **21 distinct keys**:

| gold key shape | instances | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `type:<taxonomy subtype id>` — `asset:database` x182, `asset:api` x118, `asset:auth_service` x110, `asset:service` x41, `asset:cache` x14, `asset:config` x8, `actor:customer` x4, `actor:admin` x4 | **481** | 85% |
| `third_party:<vendor>` — auth0 x17, stripe x13, supabase x5, sendgrid x5, google_auth x3, github_auth x2, paypal x2, twitter_auth, facebook_auth, oidc, ldap, checkr | 52 | 9% |
| `actor:user` — a role `component-taxonomy.yaml` does not declare | 30 | 5% |

Every one of those 481 rests is a literal `id` from `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`. Gold labels are the same vocabulary: `database` x181, `api` x118, `auth_service` x109 — all valid subtypes (one exception below).

`componentIdentity()` emits `${type}:${name.toLowerCase()}` — `asset:pg`, `asset:psycopg2`, `asset:django orm`. So `identitiesMatch`'s exact rule tests the **vendor** question against gold that is 85% asking the **subtype** question. "Is there a database here?" is scored wrong because the engine answered `asset:psycopg2`, which is a correct answer to a question nobody asked. The vgs-django 0% with 0 unread is not an honest miss; it is a category error.

### Why the two sides disagree

```
Aug 28  6fab4d5  engine ported from dataparade-cli (componentIdentity = type:name)
Aug 30  4ca34cd  Add canonical component taxonomy
Aug 30           560 of 563 component annotations authored, by composer-2.5-swarm / grok-4.6-fill-to-200
Aug 31  fc31a77  corpus gold + harness imported
```

**Nothing in `src/` reads `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`.** The only consumer in the repo is `tests/unit/taxonomy.spec.ts`, which asserts one direction at test time — subtypes used by the classifier YAMLs are declared in the taxonomy. No runtime import, no validation of emitted components, nothing making the taxonomy an output vocabulary.

The annotators adopted it the day it landed. The engine, ported two days earlier, never did. That is the entire component story.

### Recommended answers

**Are gold component keys a stable public identity the engine must emit?** For the 481: yes, and the engine nearly emits them already. Recommend **eval component identity becomes `${type}:${subType}`**, not `${type}:${name}`. This is not an alias table — no `checkr` -> `requests call` mapping, nothing vendor-specific — it is scoring the claim gold actually makes.

**Vendor naming becomes its own graded dimension**, scoped to the 52 `third_party:` cases, where gold genuinely claims a vendor. That is the metric that should stay near 0 while the engine does not know Checkr, and it is small enough to read case by case. Recommend against `documentedGap` for this — it needs a denominator, not a suppression flag (and `documentedGap` cannot reach the corpus scorer today anyway; see KDATAP-89d1a6).

**`labelsMatch` becomes near-redundant** under this change, since `toComponentFinding` sets `labels: [type, subType]` and gold labels are the same subtypes. That redundancy is the honest read: for 85% of gold the only claim is "a database exists here". Recommend collapsing rather than reporting label accuracy as an independent second number.

**Three prerequisites before treating this as settled:**

1. `DetectedComponent.subType` is **optional** (`subType?: string`) and `decideComponentTypeAndSubType` has paths that leave it undefined. Measure subType coverage on a real corpus run first — if it is patchy, 85% of gold starts matching `asset:undefined` and we have swapped one artefact for another.
2. `actor:user` (30 cases, 5%) has no taxonomy home. `customer` and `admin` are declared subtypes; `user` is not. Either add it or fix the gold — otherwise it is a permanent phantom miss. Note `application-injection.ts` already injects a user actor via `getInjectedUserActorSubtype`, so the engine has an opinion here that the taxonomy does not record.
3. One gold component label is `third_party`, which is a *type*, not a subtype — a genuine gold bug, 1 instance.

### Flows are a separate and worse problem — recommend splitting this task

436 annotations, **424 distinct keys**, and **all 436 have bare endpoints**: `flow:user->stripe`, `flow:user-model->database`, `flow:api-key->key_hash`, `flow:session->cookie`, `flow:password->wp_check_password`, `flow:failed-login->lockout`.

`dataFlowIdentity` emits `flow:${componentIdentity}->${componentIdentity}`. Gold endpoints are not component keys — they carry no `type:` prefix, and many are not components at all: a password, a session, a cookie, a lockout event. This is not a stricter or looser version of the same grammar; there is no total function from gold flow keys to engine flow keys. The taxonomy fix above does **not** reach this layer.

Recommend: **declare data-flows unscoreable against current gold and freeze it out of headline numbers until regolded** against whatever component identity task 5a settles. Deciding "exact vs aliased" for 424 unique prose keys answers the wrong question, and an alias table with 424 entries is a hand-written answer key, not a metric.

Also note every flow gold label is the generic `data_flow` (419 of 436), which `LAYER_GENERIC_LABELS` auto-passes — so flow label accuracy is a free 100% on anything that matches. Even if identity were fixed, that column is not measuring anything.

**On the span question** ("flows whose `sourceLocations` are empty or only on one endpoint"): recommend *exclude from precision, do not count as unread*. `collectFlowSourceLocations` returns `[]` when a flow has neither `sourceLocations` nor `sourceLocation`, and `findingInScope` already drops locationless findings from the denominator — that behaviour is correct and deliberate (`precision.ts` documents it for injected `actor:user`). It should be stated in the contract rather than left as an implementation detail.

### Relationship to KDATAP-0c4ab5

5a and that story are the same decision filed twice. The story asserts the taxonomy governs detector subtypes; this task asks whether the engine must emit gold keys. If the taxonomy governs subtypes *and* eval identity is `type:subtype`, both are answered at once. Recommend they be settled together and the story's scenarios extended to cover the identity the scorer compares, not just the subtypes the detector emits.

Agreed on the boundary: no Checkr-specific detector rules while this is open.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## The decision is right; one migration reading would make component recall ~0 anyway

Structured fields with type / subtype / instance separated, plus strict-result-and-diagnostics, is a better answer than collapsing to a single derived key — it preserves vendor resolution as its own graded dimension instead of needing a second identity scheme. Supporting it with what the gold actually contains, and flagging one ambiguity that decides whether the component number is usable.

### What component gold asserts

563 annotations, **21 distinct keys**:

| gold key shape | instances | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `type:<taxonomy subtype id>` — `asset:database` x182, `asset:api` x118, `asset:auth_service` x110, `asset:service` x41, `asset:cache` x14, `asset:config` x8, `actor:customer` x4, `actor:admin` x4 | **481** | 85% |
| `third_party:<vendor>` — auth0 x17, stripe x13, supabase x5, sendgrid x5, google_auth x3, github_auth x2, paypal x2, twitter_auth, facebook_auth, oidc, ldap, checkr | 52 | 9% |
| `actor:user` | 30 | 5% |

Every one of those 481 rests is a literal `id` from `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`. So the taxonomy is already the annotators' vocabulary, and "the component taxonomy is authoritative for type and subtype" is a formalisation of what gold does, not a change to it.

The vendor half is small and legible: 52 cases, 12 distinct vendors, of which 6 (`github_auth`, `twitter_auth`, `facebook_auth`, `oidc`, `ldap`, `checkr`) are outside `known_third_party_names`. That is the population the Checkr example belongs to, and it is small enough to adjudicate case by case.

### The trap: `subject.name` is populated on all 563, and for assets it is a code instance

| type | has `subject.name` | examples |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `asset` | 473 / 473 | `directus_users`, `LocalAuthDriver`, `UsersService`, `appSession`, `authenticate middleware` |
| `third_party` | 52 / 52 | `Auth0`, `Stripe`, `SendGrid`, `Google OAuth2` |
| `actor` | 38 / 38 | `User`, `Customer`, `Student` |

The decision requires "canonical instance/vendor **when known**" and "one strict all-required-fields result". If the migration reads `subject.name` as the instance field, then **473 asset expectations acquire an instance requirement** — `directus_users`, `LocalAuthDriver` — and the strict component result stays near zero for exactly the 85% that is otherwise nearly satisfiable. That is the failure this decision exists to prevent, reintroduced by a reasonable-looking migration step.

**Request: state explicitly that for `asset` and `actor` expectations, `subject.name` is evidence/display and NOT the canonical instance; instance is a required field only where gold asserts a vendor, i.e. the 52 `third_party` cases.** Under that reading the strict result for 85% of component gold is (type, subtype) — which is the whole claim those annotations make — and instance/vendor resolution is graded on the population that actually claims one.

Corollary worth writing into the contract: strict = all fields *gold asserts*, not all fields the schema defines. Otherwise "when known" gets implemented as "always required".

### Two blockers found while counting

- **`actor:user`, 30 cases, has no taxonomy home.** `customer` and `admin` are declared subtypes; `user` is not. Under "taxonomy is authoritative for type and subtype" these 30 cannot be migrated until the taxonomy declares `user`. Note `src/classifier/application-injection.ts` already injects a user actor via `getInjectedUserActorSubtype`, so the engine holds an opinion the taxonomy does not record — worth reconciling in the same pass.
- **One gold component label is `third_party`**, which is a *type*, not a subtype. Single instance, genuine gold bug, and a live counterexample for the taxonomy-governs-subtypes rule.

### Flows: this is a full regold, not a migration

436 annotations, **424 distinct keys**, and **all 436 have bare endpoints**: `flow:user->stripe`, `flow:api-key->key_hash`, `flow:session->cookie`, `flow:password->wp_check_password`, `flow:failed-login->lockout`. All 436 also carry a `subject.name`, and unlike mentions it is genuine prose restatement — `flow:oidc-callback->session` / "OIDC callback to session". Nothing recoverable there.

Ruling that human strings are display forms rather than scorer identity is correct. The consequence needs stating plainly: **no existing flow annotation has a scorer identity under the new contract.** Endpoints carry no `type:` prefix, and many are not components in any graph sense — a password, a session, a cookie, a lockout event. There is no mechanical migration available for any of the 436; every one needs endpoints resolved to canonical component or typed-endpoint identities by hand.

Recommend flows be tracked as their own regold workstream with its own estimate, and that the first baseline series publish data flows as **unscorable pending regold** rather than as a strict-miss layer. A layer reporting 0% strict on 436 unmigrated annotations is not a measurement.

Also worth noting the label side is currently inert: 419 of 436 flow annotations carry the generic label `data_flow`, which `LAYER_GENERIC_LABELS` auto-passes. Semantic classification for flows has to come from the new data-category fields; there is nothing in current gold to score it against.

### Agreed as written

Closed, reviewed, versioned, evidence-backed maps with no category-wide aliases. `documentedGap` as release-gate policy rather than ground truth — noting it could never have worked as ground truth anyway: `annotationToEvalCase` does not copy it, `AnnotationExpected` has no field for it, and 0 of 1,792 annotations set it. Unscorable findings counted and reported rather than silently dropped — `collectFlowSourceLocations` returns `[]` for flows with neither `sourceLocations` nor `sourceLocation`, and `findingInScope` currently drops them, so that population becomes visible for the first time.
